item.title: Kishiwada Danjiri Matsuri: The Runaway-Float Festival — Guide
item.description: The Kishiwada Danjiri Matsuri, held each September in the coastal city of Kishiwada, is the most exhilarating and famously reckless festival in Osaka. Teams of hundreds haul danjiri — massive, intricately carved wooden floats weighing several tonnes — through the town not in stately procession but at a flat-out run, the great skill and danger coming at the corners, where the pullers whip the float around a sharp turn without slowing while a leader dances on the roof.

item.title: Aizu Autumn Festival: A Samurai Procession Through History — Guide
item.description: The Aizu Autumn Festival is one of Tohoku’s largest historical re-enactment events, held each September in Aizu-Wakamatsu. Its centrepiece is a spectacular samurai procession — hundreds of participants in authentic-style armour, including a portrayal of feudal lord Gamo Ujisato, march through the city streets toward Tsurugajo Castle, alongside performances honouring the tragic Byakkotai cadets. The three-day festival also features traditional music, dance and food stalls throughout the historic city centre.

item.title: Jozenji Street Jazz Festival: Free Music on Every Corner — Guide
item.description: The Jozenji Street Jazz Festival is Japan’s largest street-level jazz festival, held every September when hundreds of amateur and semi-professional bands set up free outdoor stages across Sendai’s downtown streets, parks and plazas. Unlike ticketed festivals, the entire event is free — visitors simply wander between dozens of simultaneous performances along the tree-lined Jozenji-dori boulevard and surrounding streets, sampling everything from traditional jazz to fusion and Latin sounds. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Jozenji-dori & central Sendai, Miyagi Hours Weekend in mid-September, daytime Admission Free Time needed Half day to full day Best time Mid-September (festival weekend) What to See Hundreds of free outdoor performances across downtown Sendai.

item.title: Hokkaido Autumn Foliage Guide: Best Spots & Time (Sep–Oct)
item.description: Autumn comes first to Hokkaido — Japan’s earliest foliage flames into life on the high peaks in September, weeks ahead of the mainland, before sweeping down to the lakes, valleys and city parks through October. The island’s huge wild landscapes make for spectacular koyo: golden birch and larch, crimson maples and mountain ash against volcanic peaks and mirror-still caldera lakes. From the alpine slopes of Daisetsuzan to the gorges of Sounkyo and the onsen valley of Jozankei, Hokkaido’s autumn is a quieter, wilder counterpoint to Kyoto’s crowds.

item.title: Sapporo Autumn Fest Guide: Hokkaido Food Festival (Sep)
item.description: Every September, Odori Park fills with the smells of grilling seafood, sizzling meat and fresh produce for the Sapporo Autumn Fest (Sapporo Autumn Festival) — a glorious celebration of Hokkaido’s harvest and one of Japan’s great food events. For several weeks, the park’s blocks become themed gourmet zones showcasing the bounty of the island: crab and scallops, ramen, jingisukan, soup curry, dairy, sweets, sake and local wine, region by region. With long tables, autumn weather and the whole island’s cuisine in one place, it’s a food lover’s dream and a delicious way to round off summer.
